note: Mercury Editor Templates adds reusable section templates via the me_template CONTENT entity (base table me_template; revisionable, owner-tracked). No config schema. Ships seven permissions (administer/access overview/create/view/edit/delete/use mercury editor templates). The key runtime permission 'use mercury editor templates' makes published (status=1) templates appear in Mercury's add-component menu via a LayoutParagraphsAllowedTypesEvent subscriber. Routes: collection /admin/content/me-template, add /me-template/add, settings entity.me_template.settings at /admin/structure/me-template, save_as_template and insert_template. Medium/hard cases are grounded in the real me_template entity: introspection reads back a created template's label/publish status; execution creates a template and verifies it against live storage. Scripts drush en the submodule and delete test templates to restore baseline.

evals.prompt: In the mercury_editor_templates module, how does an editor turn a Mercury Editor section into something reusable, and what entity type stores those reusable templates?
evals.expected_output: Editors use 'Save as template' (route mercury_editor_templates.save_as_template) to save the selected Layout Paragraphs section; templates are stored as me_template content entities and can be re-inserted.

evals.prompt: Which permission from mercury_editor_templates must an editor have for published templates to appear in the Mercury Editor 'add component' menu?
evals.expected_output: The 'use mercury editor templates' permission. Without it the LayoutParagraphsAllowedTypesEvent subscriber returns early and no templates are offered.

evals.prompt: Where do you manage (list) all saved Mercury Editor templates, and are templates stored as configuration or as content?
evals.expected_output: Manage them at the collection /admin/content/me-template. Templates are content entities (me_template), not configuration; there is no config schema.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a Mercury Editor template saved. Inspect the live me_template entities and tell me the label of the existing template.
evals.expected_output: There is one me_template entity with label 'ME Known Template'. Query storage 'me_template' (e.g. loadMultiple) to read it.

evals.prompt: This site has two Mercury Editor templates: one is published and one is an unpublished draft. Inspect the live me_template entities and tell me the label of the PUBLISHED one.
evals.expected_output: The published template (status=1) is 'ME Pub Template'; the other, 'ME Draft Template', has status=0. Query me_template storage and check the status field.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (mercury_editor_templates is enabled), create a Mercury Editor template (me_template entity) with the label exactly 'ME Task Template' and make sure it is PUBLISHED. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A me_template entity with label 'ME Task Template' and status=1 exists (created via the me_template add form /me-template/add or entity storage create()->save()).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create a Mercury Editor template (me_template) named exactly 'ME Hero Draft' that is UNPUBLISHED (a draft). Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A me_template entity with label 'ME Hero Draft' and status=0 (unpublished) exists.
